title: Raids 3 Solo EXPERT World Record (Pre-Buff) OSRS
summary: Gnomonkey's live-streamed Solo Expert Tombs of Amascut run with no food, finishing in 22:15 overall and 20:22.20 challenge time, which he says retook the world record by 15 seconds about an hour before the update that made Raids 3 far easier. Commentary is mostly live reactions, with a few notes on the boss splits.

outline.text: Start of the raid and early chat banter about entry mode
Chat skit about a RuneScape wedding date
Akkha boss fight and damage taken

claims.text: Gnomonkey's Solo Expert Tombs of Amascut run with no food whatsoever finished in 22:15 overall and 20:22.20 challenge time, pre-buff, as stated in the description.
Before this run the Solo Expert world record on the leaderboard was 22:30 flat, and Gnomonkey beat it by 15 seconds.
Gnomonkey says it took a couple of days to get his world record back, and that he snagged it an hour before the update that made Raids 3 far easier, with the improved Tumeken's shadow.
Gnomonkey says running Solo Expert mode with no food whatsoever is no joke, and expects someone to soon take the record with the improved Tumeken's shadow.
The run was done live on Twitch, and Gnomonkey says he had been streaming non-stop since Raids 3 released.
After the record run Gnomonkey says his splits for Zebak, Baba, Akkha and Kephri were very fast and close to his best, while the Wardens were a little below average.
Gnomonkey says he lost about 20 seconds to the crocodile (Zebak) puzzle fight and did not care because he still got the world record.
Gnomonkey says the world record was back in his hands after seeing it on the leaderboard.
In the record run Gnomonkey says he took a lot of damage at Akkha, which was not ideal, and that Akkha stayed on a style he wanted to change back from.
Gnomonkey says a Toxic blowpipe is not that much worse in DPS than Tumeken's shadow at Akkha, so a style that did not return to red was okay.
Gnomonkey says the Akkha fight in this run was the fastest he had ever gone.
